Furthermore, a discounted cash flow analysis highlights an intrinsic value of Rs 230 per share, leaving a massive margin of safety of 81.2% [E31, E32], with the current market price only requiring an unrealistic -5.3% earnings growth [E33]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -53 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside a drop in trailing twelve month sales growth of -17% [E15, E24]. Nevertheless, the company outperforms sector benchmarks across key return metrics including ROA, ROE, and ROCE [E8, E9, E10], while capital expenditures scale up through a 400.0% increase in CWIP to fuel future growth [E28].

Despite headline valuation multiples appearing low, Yashhtej Industries (India) Ltd conceals severe underlying cash generation and liquidity risks [E1, E2]. Most critically, cash conversion for March 2026 sits at a disastrous -4.08x, driven by a massive negative operating cash flow of Rs -53 Cr and a free cash flow drain of Rs -73 Cr [E23, E24, E25]. This severe cash burn coincides with a sharp deterioration in top-line growth, evidenced by a -17% contraction in compounded sales over the trailing twelve months [E15]. Furthermore, borrowings have more than doubled to Rs 96 Cr in March 2026 up from Rs 40 Cr a year earlier, pushing up debt obligations alongside a warning that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E27, E39]. Compounding these operational strains, the stock languishes near the bottom of its yearly range at just 14% of its 52-week span, and despite reporting profits, the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E5, E38].
